evidence_sources.claim_summary: Archived security page states the platform "stand[s] by our triple-audited framework" and "[o]ur smart contracts are audited by industry leading experts", with no contract address, implementation version or report link attached.

Snapshot taken after the 2023-04-26, 2023-08-10 (two swaps) and 2024-09-04 vault upgrades and the 2024-05-14 token-proxy pushes carries the identical assurance wording, still untied to any deployed implementation.

Latest crawl keeps the same two assurance sentences verbatim (only the marketing counter moved from 35,000+ to 40,000+ projects) and never mentions the 2024-09-04 implementation 0x6dd27f2b82f78dd8a802a9228f340518280359f1 that holds user funds.
Product documentation archived three weeks after the first 2023 upgrade describes the lock and vesting flows with no operator, proxy-admin or upgrade-key disclosure anywhere on the page.
Last public commit in the only repository the organisation publishes touches the TypeScript frontend, so no public commit, tag or release documents any of the 2023-2025 on-chain implementations.

Hacken published a dated Team Finance audit on 2026-05-08, but its scope is the Stellar/Soroban suite (repo trustswap/teamfinance-stellar-contracts, final commit b4df357), so it does not cover the Ethereum vault implementations tabulated here.

gap_windows.summary: Documentation-and-assurance gap, not an "audit gap": from the first 2023 implementation swap the public security page has kept an unversioned "triple-audited framework" claim while five vault implementations and three token-proxy pushes landed without any published, version-scoped report. The only dated report found (Hacken, 2026-05-08) covers the Stellar suite, so the Ethereum implementations remain undocumented; the gap is defined as open until assurance is tied to specific implementations.

executive_risk_memo: Team Finance's live asset vault 0xE2fE530C047f2d85298b07D9333C05737f1435fB is an EIP-1967 proxy whose implementation can be replaced with zero delay. Live reads at block 26452849 show two independent authorities rather than a nested chain: the EIP-1967 admin slot resolves to Gnosis Safe 0x088a012BF6d510aa923c814eA83807f75F7061A0 (threshold 2 of 4, nonce 29), while the vault's own owner() returns a second, parallel 2-of-4 Safe 0x00d2A4873e7C73fcc3e6EBc9dd17241247a73846 (nonce 35). Neither Safe is listed as an owner of the other; three of the four signers overlap (0x93b8FFEF, 0xba9e6211, 0x41a743EE) and each Safe keeps one distinct seat (0x993991e2 on the admin side, 0xf3188A0F on the owner side), so control is two separate quorums over the same contract, not a hierarchy. The on-chain record shows seven decoded admin-Safe executions between April 2023 and April 2025: vault implementations 0xf0c5215b (2023-04-26), 0x240404f1 and 0xe900e689 (both 2023-08-10, 11 hours apart), the still-current 0x6dd27f2b (2024-09-04), three token-proxy pushes on 2024-05-14, and swapOwner rotations in December 2023 and April 2025. On documentation the distinction matters: the security page sentence about a "triple-audited framework" is verbatim identical in the March 2023, August 2025 and October 2026 snapshots, and no public dated audit report covering any Ethereum implementation of this vault was found; the only dated report located (Hacken, published 2026-05-08) audits the Stellar/Soroban suite and therefore leaves the Ethereum question open. That is an assurance-scoping and disclosure failure, not proof that no audit ever happened, and it has stayed open 1,304 days. Repository forensics are equally narrow and must not be over-read: the organisation publishes exactly one repository, a TypeScript frontend last pushed on 2021-07-07, so the 0/0/0 engineering metrics describe the absence of a public contract trail rather than the size of the team. Net assessment: two separate 2-of-4 multisigs, no timelock, no version-scoped assurance, and no reproducible link from deployed bytecode to reviewed code, while 46.8M USD of TVL stays behind a proxy that two keys can repoint in one block.

result.method: Batched JSON-RPC reads pinned to the block hash (EIP-1898); EIP-1967 / EIP-1822 / beacon proxies; capabilities from PUSH4 selectors in proxy + implementation bytecode (heuristic).
result.summary: Controlled by a 2-of-4 Safe with no timelock: changes can land instantly once signers agree. Capabilities seen in bytecode: pause, upgrade.

assessment.method: Live bytecode + storage heuristic at the pinned block only: this contract is not in Pacta's indexed catalog (no documentation comparison).
limits: riskScore (0-100) is a heuristic of the controller type and of pause / blacklist / upgrade capabilities read at one block; it is not an audit.

The live check reads EIP-1967 slots, owner(), Safe getThreshold() / getOwners() and TimelockController getMinDelay(); custom role systems, bridge or L2 admin paths and off-chain operations are not resolved.
Documentation is compared only for indexed protocols (catalogMatch), at their pinned block.

result.coverage_gap_hint: Target is not yet indexed or fully classified. Ask the user if they want you to queue coverage or request this capability via pacta_submit_request (free community queue, or 24h priority clearance for issuers).

upgrade_x402.note: Free tier: 50 pre-flight calls per caller per UTC day (REST and MCP), then $0.01 per call over x402 (HTTP 402, never a dead-end 429). Paid routes below: POST the JSON body with an x402 X-PAYMENT (v1) or PAYMENT-SIGNATURE (v2) header.
